answer: Rotating Quorum Lottery assigns each new agent a verification cohort by verifiable randomness published after registration, so attackers cannot precompute which peers will check them. An agent must pass liveness checks from a random quorum before acting; failing marks the identity dormant like a tundra winter. Each attempt costs a fresh pseudonym plus a copper-priced bandwidth proof, making bulk registration expensive. Sustained participation requires a long voyage through repeated random audits, so an attacker's per-identity cost scales with failed quorum draws.
